parsed_profile.title: RO COMPRESSOR BLADE AXIAL RETENTION (STAKING) ALTERNATIVES
parsed_profile.reason_for_revision: To update the 7F and 9F casing lifting and removal requirements.
parsed_profile.purpose: To inform operators of the limitations of traditional means of axial retention (peening/staking) for compressor stage 0 rotor blades (ROs) resulting from successive R0 change-outs, and to notify users of a recommended wheel modification to apply when the traditional means of retention is no longer available. This alternative method uses replacement inserts as a staking medium that has no limitation on the number of times it can be replaced.
parsed_profile.compliance_category_text: Maintenance - Identifies maintenance guidelines or best practices for reliable equipment operation.
parsed_profile.coarse_outage_type: At Scheduled Component Part Repair or Replacement
scope_of_work: For 6F units: Removal of the UH inlet bellmouth is required
For 7F and 9F units: The UH of the inlet bellmouth must be jacked ~18" off the horizontal joint or may be removed
Machining of FSS R0 dovetail slots (1x to 32x depending on scope) for the staking inserts
R0 removal/installation and staking performed by blade technicians from a GE Service Center
Two milling technicians from GE certified repair shop per shift
One NDT technician needed per shift
One Field Engineer and scaffolding crew (three craft laborers) needed
Turning gear/rotating fixture operator (dedicated person) needed
service_recommendation_line_items: Apply replacement staking insert modification to any operator planning to change R0 blades for the third or greater time, if the modification has not previously been applied
Modification should be performed in conjunction with the planned R0 change-out, or at a suitable maintenance opportunity preceding this
Depending on scope and unit conditions, all blades in the stage may need to be removed for tooling access
Do not use pressure face staking marks or blade platform flow path surface staking as alternative staking locations - these are no longer recommended
Contact GE Services representative to initiate the CM&U process for R0 wheel modification
parsed_profile.completion_criteria_text: This TIL is considered complete when the biscuit modification has been installed.
parsed_profile.maintenance_trigger_text: Third or greater replacement of the R0 blades, when traditional staking locations on the Forward Stub Shaft are exhausted.
recommended_interval_or_trigger: At Scheduled Component Part Repair or Replacement (Timing Code 5)
Third or greater R0 blade replacement
parsed_profile.hardware_or_part_configuration_text: Compressor stage 0 rotor blades (R0), Forward Stub Shaft (FSS), R0 dovetail slots, replaceable staking inserts
parsed_profile.exclusions_or_non_applicable_conditions_: Modification is usually needed on the third or greater replacement of the R0 blades; units that have not yet exhausted traditional staking locations may not require this modification.
parsed_profile.prerequisite_outage_or_inspection_contex: Modification should be performed in conjunction with the planned R0 change-out, or at a suitable maintenance opportunity preceding this. For 7F and 9F units, inlet bellmouth must be jacked ~18" or removed. For 6F units, inlet bellmouth must be removed.

parts_referenced.context: Replaceable staking inserts installed in wheel slots for R0 axial retention - contact local GE Service Representative for parts

Controlled milling machinery and special milling fixtures required for accurate drilling of pockets; dual-staking tool for proper staking geometry and placement - provided by GE Service Center technicians

configuration_variables: Number of prior R0 blade replacements
Number of R0 blades requiring modification (1x to 32x)
parsed_profile.configuration_summary: The scope of work differs by frame type: 6F units require inlet bellmouth removal, while 7F and 9F units require the inlet bellmouth to be jacked ~18" or removed. The modification is applicable when traditional staking locations are exhausted, typically after two prior R0 replacements. If staking locations are exhausted from all 32 R0 blades, replacing a single R0 blade may warrant removal of all 32 for the modification.
severity_signals: Traditional staking methods no longer recommended
Alternative staking locations (pressure face, platform flow path) no longer recommended practice
failure_consequences: Loss of axial retention for compressor stage 0 rotor blades if traditional staking locations are exhausted and no alternative is applied
Reduced equipment reliability if interim staking methods (pressure face or platform flow path) are used instead of the recommended insert modification
parsed_profile.risk_summary: If traditional staking locations on the Forward Stub Shaft are exhausted after successive R0 blade replacements and the recommended insert modification is not applied, there is risk of inadequate axial retention of compressor R0 blades. Previously used alternative staking locations (pressure face and platform flow path surface) are no longer recommended.

This TIL is considered complete when the biscuit modification has been installed.
GE recommends this modification to any operator planning to change RO blades for the third or greater time, if the modification has not previously been applied.
For 7F and 9F units: The UH of the inlet bellmouth must be jacked ~ 18" off the horizontal joint or may be removed.
if staking locations are exhausted from all 32 R0 blades, the need to replace a single R0 blade may warrant removal of all 32 such that the modification can be conducted on the entire wheel.
To update the 7F and 9F casing lifting and removal requirements.
